variations.name: Green methanol vessels, engines & fuel supply
variations.description: Ships burn e-methanol (from renewable power) or bio-methanol (from waste) in dual-fuel diesel engines, cutting greenhouse gas up to ~75-95% with a liquid fuel that is easy to store and bunker — vessels and engines are commercial, but green fuel supply is the binding constraint.

companies.name: MAN Energy Solutions
companies.what: Dominant supplier of ME-LGIM two-stroke dual-fuel methanol engines that power Maersk's fleet and most of the global methanol orderbook.
companies.signal: Methanol dual-fuel engine of choice for hundreds of ordered vessels since the Laura Maersk (2023)

companies.name: A.P. Moller - Maersk
companies.what: First-mover container line: world's first methanol-fueled boxship (Laura Maersk), first large dual-fuel series, and first big-ship methanol retrofit conversion.
companies.signal: Completed world's first series of large dual-fuel methanol vessels (Axel Maersk, 2025); ~25 methanol-enabled ships ordered

companies.name: European Energy
companies.what: Built and operates Kassø (Denmark), the world's first commercial-scale e-methanol plant (42,000 t/yr, 51/49 with Mitsui), supplying Maersk, LEGO and Novo Nordisk.
companies.signal: Kassø inaugurated May 2025; first e-methanol bunkering of Laura Maersk; green bridge financing with Mitsui Jan 2026

companies.name: Liquid Wind
companies.what: Swedish developer of standardized ~100,000 t/yr e-methanol plants (FlagshipONE, sold to Ørsted and later cancelled).
companies.signal: Raised ~€64M but filed for bankruptcy May 2026 after failing to secure offtakes/financing; subsidiaries put up for sale

companies.name: C2X
companies.what: A.P. Moller Holding spin-out developing multi-megaton green methanol production in Egypt, Spain and the US Gulf (Beaver Lake, Louisiana).
companies.signal: $100M investment from ENEOS alongside APMH/Maersk; ambition of 3 Mt/yr capacity by 2030

companies.name: WasteFuel
companies.what: Converts municipal and agricultural waste into bio-methanol for marine fuel.
companies.signal: Backed by Maersk Growth and BP ($10M plus offtake MoU); launched biomethanol sales

companies.name: Methanex
companies.what: World's largest methanol producer and marine methanol supplier; operates the methanol-fueled Waterfront Shipping tanker fleet.
companies.signal: Acquired OCI Global's international methanol business (~$2B deal closed 2025), consolidating fuel supply

companies.name: X-Press Feeders
companies.what: Operates Europe's first green-methanol-powered container feeder network (Rotterdam-Baltic GFX/GBX routes) with ISCC-certified fuel.
companies.signal: 3 dual-fuel feeders operating, 14 ordered (deliveries through 2026)

variations.white_space: Ships have outrun fuel: one commercial e-methanol plant (42 kt/yr) versus megaton-scale fleet demand, and developers die without bankable offtakes (Liquid Wind bankruptcy, Ørsted's FlagshipONE cancellation). The opening is for producers who can lock long-term offtakes and shrink the green premium, plus FuelEU-compliance structures that monetize it.

variations.name: Ammonia propulsion & ammonia-to-power
variations.description: Ammonia is a carbon-free hydrogen carrier that can be burned in dual-fuel engines or cracked into hydrogen for fuel cells, promising zero-CO2 deep-sea shipping if toxicity, N2O slip and bunkering infrastructure are solved.

companies.name: MAN Energy Solutions
companies.what: Developing the two-stroke ammonia engine (ME-LGIA) expected to power the deep-sea ammonia fleet.
companies.signal: First ammonia dual-fuel engine deliveries scheduled early 2026

companies.name: WinGD
companies.what: First to put a large two-stroke ammonia dual-fuel engine (X72DF-A, ~5% pilot fuel) into a delivered ocean-going ship.
companies.signal: First ammonia dual-fuel vessel delivered to Exmar (built at HD Hyundai Mipo); engines delivering from Q4 2025

companies.name: Wärtsilä
companies.what: Launched the first commercial four-stroke ammonia engine (Wärtsilä 25 Ammonia) for short-sea vessels.
companies.signal: First newbuild installations for Viridis Bulk Carriers and Skarv Shipping; equipment deliveries from Q4 2026

companies.name: Amogy
companies.what: Cracks ammonia onboard into hydrogen for fuel cells; sailed the world's first ammonia-powered vessel (NH3 Kraken tug, 2024) and now targets ships plus floating power.
companies.signal: Raised $80M in 2025 (~$300M total), led by Korea Development Bank; Asia maritime expansion

companies.name: Azane Fuel Solutions
companies.what: Builds containerized and floating ammonia bunkering terminals — the missing fueling infrastructure layer.
companies.signal: World-first ammonia bunkering terminal safety permit in Norway; 15 units pre-ordered by Yara Clean Ammonia

companies.name: Yara Clean Ammonia
companies.what: World's largest ammonia trader, building Yara Eyde — the first ammonia-powered container ship (with North Sea Container Line) — plus bunkering supply.
companies.signal: Yara Eyde steel cut Sept 2025 at Qingdao Yangfan; delivery ~mid-2026 for Oslo-Rotterdam route

companies.name: Exmar
companies.what: First shipowner to take delivery of ocean-going ammonia dual-fuel gas carriers (which can burn their own cargo).
companies.signal: World's first ammonia dual-fuel midsize gas carriers named/delivered in South Korea in 2025

companies.name: Fortescue
companies.what: Converted the Green Pioneer, the world's first ammonia dual-fuel demonstration vessel, to force regulatory and port acceptance.
companies.signal: Demonstrated ammonia operation in Singapore (2024) and showcased the vessel internationally

variations.white_space: Engine supply is consolidating with the three incumbent engine houses; the open gaps are port-side bunkering networks, crew safety/training systems and N2O abatement — whoever industrializes safe ammonia transfer owns the bottleneck.

variations.name: Hydrogen & fuel-cell vessels
variations.description: Compressed or liquid hydrogen feeding PEM fuel cells gives genuinely zero-emission propulsion for ferries, harbor craft and inland barges, but low energy density and high green-hydrogen cost confine it to short, subsidized routes — and the sector has suffered heavy attrition.

companies.name: Norled
companies.what: Operates MF Hydra, the world's first liquid-hydrogen ferry (Ballard fuel cells), in Norway since March 2023.
companies.signal: In service since 2023, but Norled booked ~NOK 1B (~€85M) of losses partly tied to its hydrogen bet

companies.name: Torghatten Nord
companies.what: Building the world's two largest hydrogen ferries (117 m, 120 cars) for Norway's Bodø-Lofoten Vestfjorden route, 85% hydrogen operation.
companies.signal: Ferries in production with >6 MW PowerCell systems each; service slipped from Oct 2025 into 2026

companies.name: PowerCell Group
companies.what: Swedish marine fuel-cell maker supplying megawatt-scale systems, including the Torghatten Nord ferries and the first commercial marine methanol-to-power system.
companies.signal: World's largest marine fuel-cell order; first commercial 2 MW methanol-to-power sale (Nov 2025)

companies.name: Ballard Power Systems
companies.what: FCwave marine fuel-cell modules powered MF Hydra and the FPS hydrogen barges.
companies.signal: Marine modules in service since 2023; company restructured 2024-25 amid weak hydrogen demand

companies.name: e1 Marine
companies.what: Methanol-to-hydrogen reformers that generate fuel-cell-grade hydrogen onboard, sidestepping hydrogen storage and bunkering.
companies.signal: Eight M30 reformers ordered for PowerCell's first commercial 2 MW methanol-to-power system (Nov 2025)

companies.name: Genevos
companies.what: French maker of modular marine PEM Hydrogen Power Modules (15-90 kW, stackable) for workboats and passenger vessels.
companies.signal: High-power range launched 2024; world-first hydrogen retrofit passenger vessel project launched 2025

companies.name: Zero Emission Industries
companies.what: Hydrogen powertrain behind Sea Change, the first commercial hydrogen fuel-cell ferry in the US (San Francisco Bay).
companies.signal: Sea Change entered public service 2024; backed by Chevron New Energies and Crowley

companies.name: Future Proof Shipping
companies.what: Retrofitted and operated the world's first hydrogen-powered inland container barges (H2 Barge 1 & 2, hauling Nike cargo on the Rhine).
companies.signal: Technology worked but economics failed; declared bankrupt June 2026

companies.name: TECO 2030
companies.what: Norwegian developer of marine fuel-cell stacks with a planned gigafactory in Narvik.
companies.signal: Bankrupt Dec 2024 after losing ~$30M; could not raise the ~$35M needed to start its factory

variations.white_space: Two flagship failures (Future Proof Shipping, TECO 2030) plus Norled's heavy losses show green-hydrogen cost and missing infrastructure kill the economics wherever batteries suffice; the defensible niche is routes too long for batteries with captive or subsidized hydrogen supply — or onboard methanol reforming that dodges hydrogen logistics entirely.

variations.name: Battery-electric ships, ferries, workboats & hydrofoils
variations.description: Lithium batteries — often paired with hydrofoils that cut drag ~80% — power ferries, harbor craft, workboats and short-sea cargo with zero exhaust and lower energy cost per mile; already standard on Norwegian-style short ferry routes and spreading fast.

companies.name: Corvus Energy
companies.what: Dominant maritime energy-storage supplier (Orca, Blue Whale LFP) for ferries, offshore vessels and hybrid container ships.
companies.signal: ~25 MWh Blue Whale order for the first all-electric offshore SOV (Bibby Marine); systems on hundreds of vessels; Matson boxship wins

companies.name: Echandia
companies.what: Swedish heavy-duty LTO/LFP marine battery systems built for fast-charge, high-cycle urban ferries.
companies.signal: Battery systems powering urban e-ferry fleets including Copenhagen's Damen-built ferries

companies.name: Candela
companies.what: Carbon-fiber electric hydrofoil shuttles (P-12) and leisure boats that cut energy use ~80% versus planing hulls.
companies.signal: ~€30M raised Mar 2026 (incl. IFC) on top of $40M in 2024; P-12 in Stockholm public transit since Nov 2024; export orders (NZ, Saudi, Berlin)

companies.name: Artemis Technologies
companies.what: Belfast-based eFoiler electric hydrofoil workboats, pilot boats and 150-passenger fast ferries (EF-12, EF-24).
companies.signal: Leads ~£60M Belfast Maritime Consortium; EF-12 craft delivered to commercial customers; EF-24 ferry program underway

companies.name: Navier
companies.what: US electric hydrofoil boats (N30) aimed at water shuttles and commuting.
companies.signal: N30 operated as a Stripe employee commuter shuttle on SF Bay; expanding pilot routes

companies.name: Arc
companies.what: Vertically integrated US electric sport boats now expanding into electric tugboats.
companies.signal: Raised $70M (late 2024, backers incl. Eclipse, a16z, Lowercarbon); Arc Sport shipping; electric tug program announced

companies.name: Fleetzero
companies.what: Containerized swappable LFP battery packs and retrofit propulsion to electrify coastal cargo ships, plus marine autonomy.
companies.signal: $43M Series A (Jan 2026) led by Obvious Ventures with Maersk Growth and Breakthrough Energy; 300 MWh/yr Houston production line

companies.name: Pure Watercraft
companies.what: Seattle electric outboards and pontoon boats; GM paid $150M for a 25% stake in 2021.
companies.signal: Entered receivership July 2024 with ~900 undelivered pre-orders; assets sold off

companies.name: Incat
companies.what: Tasmanian shipbuilder of Hull 096 'China Zorrilla' — the world's largest battery-electric ship (130 m, 40+ MWh) for Buquebus.
companies.signal: Launched May 2025 for the Buenos Aires-Uruguay route; building an electric-ship product line

companies.name: COSCO Shipping / CSSC
companies.what: Built and operate the 700 TEU river-electric container ships Green Water 01/02 with containerized swappable batteries on the Yangtze.
companies.signal: Green Water 01 in commercial service since 2024 (~50 MWh with battery boxes)

variations.name: Wind-assisted propulsion: rotors, rigid wings, suction sails, kites
variations.description: Retrofittable rotor sails, rigid or inflatable wings, suction sails and kites convert free wind into 5-30% fuel savings on existing cargo ships — one of the few decarbonization levers with near-term payback under FuelEU Maritime and EU ETS.

companies.name: Norsepower
companies.what: Market-leading Flettner rotor sails for tankers, bulkers, ro-ros and ferries.
companies.signal: 32 rotors on 18 ships plus ~40 more booked (Mar 2025); new Dafeng, China factory (50 rotors/yr); VLCC newbuild orders

companies.name: Anemoi Marine Technologies
companies.what: Rotor sails with folding/rail deployment systems suited to bulk carriers (Vale's Sohar Max VLOC, Berge Meru Newcastlemax).
companies.signal: Rotors operating on the world's largest ore carriers; opened Jingjiang, China factory July 2025

companies.name: bound4blue
companies.what: Autonomous eSAIL suction sails delivering the industry's highest thrust per square meter of sail.
companies.signal: $44M raised 2025; five-tanker, 20-sail retrofit program with Maersk underway (Maersk Trieste first)

companies.name: BAR Technologies
companies.what: Rigid 37.5 m WindWings proven on Cargill's Pyxis Ocean bulker.
companies.signal: Pyxis Ocean trials averaged ~3 t/day fuel savings; follow-on orders from Union Maritime and others

companies.name: Econowind
companies.what: Containerized, foldable VentoFoil suction wings sized for short-sea ships and coasters.
companies.signal: Dozens of VentoFoil units delivered and at sea on European short-sea vessels

companies.name: Michelin (WISAMO)
companies.what: Inflatable, telescopic wingsail from Michelin R&D with full automation.
companies.signal: First commercial contract (French DGAMPA patrol vessel) signed early 2025; installation 2027

companies.name: Airseas
companies.what: Automated Seawing parafoil kite that tows ships, spun out of Airbus.
companies.signal: Fell into receivership after its Asian investor withdrew; bought out by K Line (via Oceanicwing), which is scaling the Nantes factory

companies.name: Chantiers de l'Atlantique
companies.what: Developer of SolidSail ~1,500 m2 folding carbon rigs powering Neoliner Origin and the planned Orient Express Silenseas sailing cruise ships.
companies.signal: SolidSail rigs at sea on Neoliner Origin since 2025

variations.name: Primary-sail cargo shipping lines
variations.description: New-build cargo ships using sails as primary propulsion (engines auxiliary) cut voyage emissions 80-90% and sell verified low-carbon freight for premium goods like wine, cocoa, coffee and vehicles.

companies.name: TOWT
companies.what: French line operating purpose-built 81 m cargo schooners (Anemos, Artemis) on transatlantic coffee/cocoa/wine routes.
companies.signal: Two ships in commercial service since 2024; six sisters ordered for a fleet of eight by ~2027

companies.name: Neoline
companies.what: Operates Neoliner Origin, the world's largest sail cargo ship (136 m ro-ro with SolidSail rigs, 80%+ fuel cut), St-Nazaire to Baltimore/Halifax.
companies.signal: Delivered 2025; monthly commercial transatlantic service began Oct 2025 with shippers incl. Renault and Hennessy

companies.name: Grain de Sail
companies.what: Vertically integrated French chocolate/coffee/wine brand that ships its own goods on its own sailing cargo vessels.
companies.signal: Grain de Sail II (50 t) in regular transatlantic service; larger third vessel planned

companies.name: Veer Group
companies.what: Designing 160 TEU hybrid sail container ships (Mamba) with hydrogen fuel-cell auxiliary power.
companies.signal: ABS Approval in Principle received; tendering shipyards — pre-construction stage

companies.name: Sailcargo Inc.
companies.what: Building Ceiba, a 190-tonne wooden sailing cargo ship with regenerative electric auxiliary propulsion, at its Costa Rica yard.
companies.signal: Construction running years behind schedule with launch dates repeatedly slipping; financing via small Canadian investments

companies.name: Zéphyr & Borée
companies.what: Co-developed Canopée, the sail-assisted ro-ro that carries Ariane 6 rocket components to French Guiana, and is ordering sail container ships.
companies.signal: Canopée in commercial service since 2023 with four Oceanwings wingsails

variations.white_space: Small capacity and ~11-knot speeds cap the addressable market to premium, time-tolerant cargo; FuelEU/CSRD-driven demand for verified low-CO2 freight is the opening, but nobody has cracked container-scale sail economics yet — Veer and France's Windcoop are first attempts.

variations.name: Drop-in marine biofuels & bio-LNG bunkering
variations.description: Waste-based biodiesel blends (FAME/HVO, up to B100) and liquefied biomethane drop into existing engines and bunkering infrastructure with no retrofit, delivering up to ~80-100% well-to-wake cuts and serving as the workhorse of FuelEU compliance.

companies.name: FincoEnergies (GoodFuels)
companies.what: Pioneer of 100% waste-based marine biofuel (B100) bunkering at scale; GoodFuels brand now part of FincoEnergies.
companies.signal: Acquired by FincoEnergies (2023); thousands of biofuel deliveries plus FuelEU pooling services — continues operating as a brand

companies.name: Titan Clean Fuels
companies.what: Largest independent LNG/bio-LNG bunkering company with its own bunker vessels (Alice Cosulich, Optimus).
companies.signal: Multi-delivery bio-LNG contract with MOL (Mar 2025); fueling UECC's fleet with bio-LNG since 2024; first DNV-verified FuelEU pool

companies.name: Gasum
companies.what: Nordic state-backed LNG and liquefied biomethane supplier with liquefaction plants and a bunker-vessel network across the Baltic and North Sea.
companies.signal: Expanding renewable LBM supply for shipping under FuelEU demand

companies.name: Argent Energy
companies.what: Waste-based biodiesel producer (UK/Netherlands) feeding marine B30-B100 blends at the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp bunkering hub.
companies.signal: Long-running feedstock-to-blend supplier into marine biofuels

companies.name: Chevron Renewable Energy Group
companies.what: Major waste-FAME/HVO producer supplying marine biodiesel programs.
companies.signal: Chevron acquired REG for $3.15B (2022); supplies marine blend programs

companies.name: MASH Makes
companies.what: Danish-Indian producer of carbon-negative pyrolysis bio-oil from agricultural residues, sold as marine fuel.
companies.signal: Maersk vessel trial of MASH Makes bio-oil (2024); first commercial volumes from India plant

variations.name: Onboard carbon capture
variations.description: Scrubber-like systems capture CO2 from ship exhaust (amine, calcium-looping or centrifugal processes) and store it onboard for port offload, letting existing fossil-fueled ships cut 70-95% of stack emissions without switching fuels.

companies.name: Value Maritime
companies.what: Dutch first mover selling prefab Filtree scrubber-plus-capture units with a 'CO2 battery' offloaded for reuse in greenhouses.
companies.signal: Multiple commercial installations on container feeders and tankers (incl. X-Press Feeders) since 2021

companies.name: Seabound
companies.what: Compact calcium-looping capture that binds CO2 into limestone pebbles offloaded for cement making.
companies.signal: First commercial project on the UBC Cork cement carrier with Hartmann/Heidelberg Materials (Jul 2025); up to 95% capture; ESA award

companies.name: Carbon Ridge
companies.what: Modular centrifugal amine capture that shrinks system size and energy penalty for retrofits.
companies.signal: $20M+ total raised; world-first centrifugal onboard capture deployed on Scorpio Tankers' STI Spiga (2025)

companies.name: Wärtsilä
companies.what: First incumbent to commercialize full-chain onboard CCS (capture, liquefaction, onboard storage).
companies.signal: Commercial launch May 2025 after achieving 70% capture on Solvang's Clipper Eris retrofit

companies.name: Solvang
companies.what: Norwegian gas-carrier owner running the world's first full-scale onboard CCS vessel and planning fleet rollout.
companies.signal: Clipper Eris sailing with a 7 MW capture plant since Feb 2025 (Enova-funded); newbuilds capture-ready

companies.name: STAX Engineering
companies.what: Barge-based exhaust capture serving ships at berth — port-side emissions capture with no vessel retrofit.
companies.signal: $70M raised; partnership with Seabound for CO2 processing; operating at California ports

companies.name: Daphne Technology
companies.what: Swiss maker of exhaust measurement and abatement tech (methane slip, SOx/NOx) positioning into maritime carbon management.
companies.signal: Backed by Trafigura and Shell Ventures; methane-slip systems deployed on LNG carriers

companies.name: Mitsubishi Shipbuilding
companies.what: Ran CC-Ocean, the first marine CO2 capture demonstration at sea (2021), feeding its commercial marine CCS and LCO2 carrier line.
companies.signal: CC-Ocean verified capture at sea; building liquefied CO2 carriers

variations.white_space: Capture is proven but the loop is open: there is no standardized port CO2 offload/storage chain and IMO/EU accounting for captured CO2 is still pending, so value hinges on regulation — first movers locking port logistics and cement/CCU offtake (the Seabound-Heidelberg model) own the gap.

variations.name: Nuclear maritime propulsion
variations.description: Small modular and molten-salt reactors aboard ships or floating power plants would deliver years of zero-carbon operation without refueling, but no commercial nuclear merchant vessel exists — today's work is reactor design, class rules and feasibility studies.

companies.name: Core Power
companies.what: UK/US developer commercializing molten salt reactors for floating nuclear power and ship propulsion via its US-anchored Liberty program.
companies.signal: ~$150M invested; shareholders incl. HD Hyundai, TerraPower and Wan Hai; targets $10B orderbook by 2030 and floating plants by mid-2030s

companies.name: Seaborg Technologies
companies.what: Danish compact molten salt reactor (CMSR) for power barges, partnered with Samsung Heavy Industries and KAERI.
companies.signal: SHI partnership for barges of up to 8x100 MWe; company downsized and refocused in 2023-24

companies.name: Newcleo
companies.what: Lead-cooled fast mini-reactors (30 MWe 'nuclear battery') being studied for merchant ship integration with Fincantieri and RINA.
companies.signal: Raised €500M+; Fincantieri/RINA naval feasibility study underway

companies.name: HD KSOE (HD Hyundai)
companies.what: Korean shipbuilding group designing an SMR-powered 15,000 TEU containership and a marine nuclear test facility.
companies.signal: ABS Approval in Principle for the nuclear boxship design; marine nuclear demo facility planned at Yongin; business model targeted for 2030

companies.name: Samsung Heavy Industries
companies.what: Developing CMSR floating power barges and nuclear-propelled ship concepts with KAERI and Seaborg.
companies.signal: Multiple Approvals in Principle for floating nuclear designs

companies.name: Ulstein
companies.what: Norwegian designer of the Thor concept — a thorium molten-salt 'charging ship' that would recharge battery-electric cruise vessels at sea.
companies.signal: Concept design only (2022); no build committed

variations.white_space: Physics is proven by navies, but civilian port access, insurance/liability frameworks and IMO rules don't yet exist, so credible players are few and capital-heavy; the near-term opening is floating nuclear power for ports and islands (regulated like land assets) before propulsion, plus licensing/class-rule tooling.

variations.name: Vessel & port efficiency: air lubrication, hull tech, route optimization, shore power
variations.description: Air lubrication, advanced hull coatings and cleaning robots, AI voyage optimization and shore power cut fleet fuel burn 5-30% with proven paybacks — the cheapest abatement in shipping and the multiplier that makes expensive green fuels viable.

companies.name: Silverstream Technologies
companies.what: Market-leading air lubrication system that pumps a microbubble carpet under the hull, cutting fuel 5-10% net.
companies.signal: Installed or on order for well over 100 vessels incl. 18 QC-MAX LNG carriers; FT fastest-growing lists 2023-24

companies.name: Jotun
companies.what: Hull coatings leader pairing SeaQuantum antifouling with the HullSkater robotic proactive cleaning service and performance guarantees.
companies.signal: Hull Skating Solutions deployed globally; coatings on tens of thousands of ships

companies.name: ZeroNorth
companies.what: AI voyage, bunker and emissions optimization platform spun out of Maersk Tankers.
companies.signal: Optimizes thousands of vessels; grew via multiple acquisitions (ClearLynx, Prosmar, etc.)

companies.name: Sofar Ocean
companies.what: World's largest private ocean sensor network (Spotter buoys) feeding the Wayfinder dynamic weather-routing platform.
companies.signal: $39M Series B; Wayfinder adopted by major carriers

companies.name: DeepSea Technologies
companies.what: AI vessel-performance digital twins and live route optimization (Cassandra/Pythia).
companies.signal: Acquired by Japan's Nabtesco (2022); systems running across hundreds of vessels

companies.name: Orca AI
companies.what: Computer-vision situational awareness and navigation assistant that also cuts fuel through fewer course deviations.
companies.signal: ~$23M raised in 2024; deployed across 1,000+ vessels

companies.name: Cavotec
companies.what: Shore power (cold ironing) connection systems and automated mooring that let berthed ships shut engines off.
companies.signal: Listed Swiss incumbent; shore-power systems at major ports worldwide ahead of EU's 2030 onshore-power mandate

companies.name: Graphite Innovation & Technologies (GIT Coatings)
companies.what: Graphene-based hard foul-release hull coatings (XGIT-FUEL/PROP) cutting drag, biofouling and underwater noise without biocides.
companies.signal: Commercial deployments across international fleets; venture-backed Canadian scale-out

companies.name: NAPA
companies.what: Finnish ship design, stability and voyage optimization software embedded across yards, owners and class.
companies.signal: Decades-old incumbent whose fleet intelligence and loading software runs across the global fleet
